summary: Approval token reuse after Okta account-merge prevents temporary elevation for affected users
description:
Issue summary:
Users who recently underwent Okta account merge (duplicate identities merged into single canonical account) are unable to complete self-service temporary elevation flows. The approval UI completes but the backend returns a 403 during the token exchange step. Impact: oncall and SRE asking for rapid manual elevation; several engineers blocked from emergency runbooks.

Impact:
- ~8 engineers across infra and platform teams were unable to obtain temporary elevated roles (SSH bastion, runbook edit).
- Self-service path fails; manual SRE intervention required to grant ephemeral role.
- Repro window: 2026-03-10 09:12 - 2026-03-10 12:40 UTC.

Environment:
- prod (us-east), approval-service v1.2.1, auth-proxy v2.0.0, Okta tenant redwood-prod.

Observed behavior:
- Approval UI shows success but the POST /api/v1/approve/exchange returns 403 with body: "approval_token invalid: subject_mismatch".
- Okta SAML/ID token appears valid for the session; however the approval token subject (NameID) differs from the current session subject after account merge.

Expected behavior:
- Temporary elevation should succeed if the user is now a canonical merged account that retains entitlement mappings. Approval exchange should accept subject aliasing from the account-merge path or reject upfront with clear remediation steps.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Have an Okta test subject 'alice+old@redwood.com' merged into 'alice@redwood.com' via SCIM/Okta account-merge flow.
2) Login to console via SSO (user sees session for 'alice@redwood.com').
3) Trigger self-service temporary elevation in Console -> Access Requests -> Request Elevation.
4) Complete approver flow; UI displays approval success and returns approval_token to client.
5) Client posts approval_token to /api/v1/approve/exchange and receives 403 with 'subject_mismatch' error.
6) Repeatable when approval token subject differs from current Okta NameID after account merge.
logs: 2026-03-10T09:13:21Z approval-service ERROR token-exchange: approval_token=abcDEF123 invalid: subject_mismatch (expected: okta|alice@redwood.com, got: okta|alice+old@redwood.com)
2026-03-10T09:13:22Z console WARN elevation-client: received 403 from approval-service, showing generic failure to user
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: approval-service rejects approval_token when NameID in token does not match current SSO NameID; account-merge workflow does not surface alias mapping to approval service.
Checked Okta merge logs (via /events) and found merge completed at 2026-03-10T09:12:58Z; SCIM propagation finished ~5s later.
Confirmed approval-token generation included pre-merge subject (alice+old@redwood.com) when user started flow in a session that straddled the merge timing.
Reproduced locally by simulating merge: generate approval_token for old-subject, then update session to canonical subject and attempt token exchange -> identical 403 subject_mismatch.
Auth team verified session cookies are anchored to current NameID; approval tokens contain a subject claim tied to the original SSO assertion used to request approval.
Risk: users who initiate approval flows during account-merge windows get orphaned tokens; rare but high-friction for oncall.
comments: Sofia Martinez [2026-03-10T09:25Z]: Raised by PagerDuty alert from infra-oncall. Several folks filed manual elevation requests in #oncall. Blocking emergency runbook execution.
Evan Patel [2026-03-10T09:40Z]: Reproduced in staging by performing Okta account-merge. Confirmed subject mismatch on token exchange. Will own fix; creating a short plan.

Lina Zhou (Auth) [2026-03-10T10:15Z]: Okta can preserve aliases in SCIM metadata; authorization checks currently compare strict NameID. Suggest adding alias mapping layer in approval-service as quick mitigation.

Ben Carver (SRE) [2026-03-10T10:45Z]: Temporary workaround: SRE can issue manual elevated SSO session via admin console (bypass token-exchange) while fix is implemented. Documented steps in runbook and informed #oncall.
Evan Patel [2026-03-11T02:10Z]: Implemented hotfix branch that accepts approved alias mapping header produced by auth-proxy. Running canary in us-east-prod (5% traffic).
Sofia Martinez [2026-03-12T07:32Z]: Hotfix verified: affected users reported successful elevation post-rollout. Closing incident and adding follow-up tasks.
resolution: Hotfix released in approval-service v1.2.2 -> v1.2.3: service will accept approved alias mappings surfaced by auth-proxy for a short window during account-merge events, and logs token subject alias occurrences for monitoring. Deployed as canary (5%) then 100% in prod us-east on 2026-03-11 23:45 UTC. Runbook updated with full manual-elevation workaround and detection alert for duplicate-nameid events. Follow-ups: add telemetry to Okta merge webhook consumer and create a daily alert for subject-alias occurrences. Incident closed after confirmation from affected users.
